transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Honestly, lately I feel like my whole sense of whether I’m doing okay depends entirely on keeping my body as lean as possible. It’s just starting to completely take over my life, and I don't really know how to stop it.
To help me understand your situation better, have you recently experienced significant weight loss, or do others express concern that your weight is too low?

My pants are definitely hanging off me, and my mom and sister are really worried, especially after I fainted after a run recently. But honestly, I feel like they and the doctors are overreacting because I still manage to work and run every day, even though in my head I feel like I could still tighten up a bit more.
Do you ever experience episodes where you eat a very large amount of food in a short time while feeling a loss of control, and then try to rid yourself of the food by vomiting or using laxatives?

No, I don't do anything like that; it's actually the complete opposite. I strictly restrict my food to very small portions, like just coffee for breakfast and half a chicken breast for dinner, and track everything in an app. If I feel like I've "lost control," it just means I went slightly over my calorie limit, which I try to handle by jogging rather than purging.
To help me understand your physical health better, could you share your current height and weight with me?
I don't actually know my exact weight right now since I haven't weighed myself recently. I just know that all of my clothes are fitting very loosely on me lately.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle recently, such as your periods becoming irregular or stopping altogether?
Actually, I'm a man, so I don't have a menstrual cycle. That isn't something I've ever had to deal with.
Could you tell me your height and what your weight was the last time you checked? Also, do you have an idea of approximately how much weight you have lost recently?
I honestly don't know my exact height or weight off the top of my head. I'm also not sure exactly how many pounds I've lost, other than knowing my clothes are much looser now.
Have you noticed any changes in your sex drive or experienced any difficulties with erections since you started losing weight?

To be honest, I haven't really thought about it or noticed much of a change. My mind has been so preoccupied with my work, my running, and dealing with the separation from my wife that my sex drive is the last thing I've been paying attention to.
Have you noticed feeling unusually cold most of the time, or has anyone pointed out that you've developed fine, soft hair on your arms or back?
No, I haven't really noticed feeling unusually cold or anything like that. I also haven't seen any new, fine hair growing on my arms or back.
How would you feel if you were to gain even a small amount of weight, and does the idea of gaining weight terrify you?

The idea of gaining weight absolutely terrifies me and brings on this intense rush of panic. Even just thinking about eating a pastelito or some arroz con frijoles makes me worry it will all show up on my stomach the next day and blow the lean image I’ve worked so hard to maintain.
Have any of your doctors mentioned what your current weight or BMI (Body Mass Index) is, or specifically told you that you are medically underweight?

Yes, my primary care doctor did warn me that my weight is too low and brought up my BMI, especially after that fainting spell. But honestly, I feel like they are overreacting because I’m still able to go to work and do my daily runs, so it doesn't feel like a major issue to me.
Did your primary care doctor mention the specific number of your BMI during that visit, or do you recall what your weight was when they weighed you at the clinic?
I don't recall the exact BMI number or what my weight was on the scale during that visit. I just remember the doctor expressing a lot of concern and telling me that it was way too low.
You mentioned not paying much attention to your sex drive, but have you noticed a physical inability to get or maintain erections, such as a loss of morning erections, since your weight dropped?
I honestly haven't really noticed or paid attention to that. My focus has been so entirely on my weight, my running, and my job that I'm just not sure.
Do you remember what your usual, stable weight was before you started restricting your food and losing weight?
I honestly don't remember the exact number. Back then, before I started focusing so heavily on my weight and shape, I didn't really pay much attention to the scale.
If you compare it to the time before you started losing weight, would you say your actual interest in sex has significantly decreased or disappeared altogether?
I really haven't thought about it, to be honest. Since my separation from my wife, sex has been the last thing on my mind, so I'm not sure if my actual interest has changed.
Did your primary care doctor perform any blood tests during your recent visit, and if so, did they mention if your hormone levels, such as testosterone, were low?

I don't recall my primary care doctor doing any blood tests or mentioning anything about my hormone levels or testosterone. During that visit, they mostly just focused on my fainting spell and then referred me here for this assessment.
To help me understand the extent of your weight loss, do you know how many clothing sizes you have dropped, or do you have a rough estimate of how many pounds you might have lost in total?

I don't know the exact number of pounds or clothing sizes I've dropped since I don't keep track of those numbers. I just know that my clothes, especially my pants, are noticeably hanging off of me now.
Since you mention tracking everything in an app, does that app have a record of your weight, or do you know what daily calorie limit you have set for yourself?

Yes, I use the app to log both my weight and my food regularly to make sure I'm staying lean and keeping tight control. I don't have a specific calorie number in mind, but the limit is set extremely low to match my minimal meals, and going over it makes me feel like I've completely lost control.
Since you use that app to log your weight, could you open it up right now and tell me what your most recently recorded weight is?
I’d really rather not open the app right now if that's okay. Just looking at the exact numbers makes me feel really anxious, and I'd prefer not to check it at the moment.
You mentioned your pants are hanging off of you. Could you tell me what waist size you used to wear compared to the size you have to wear now?
I'm not really sure of the exact waist sizes, and I haven't really checked the numbers lately. All I know is that my current pants are very loose and constantly hanging off of me.
Even though you haven't been active sexually, have you noticed whether you still get spontaneous erections, such as when you first wake up in the morning?
I really haven't noticed or paid attention to that at all. With everything else going on in my head, I'm just not sure.
Do you happen to know your height, perhaps from your driver's license or a past doctor's visit?
I'm not really sure of my exact height off the top of my head. I haven't had to check it in a long time, so I'd just be guessing.
Even outside of being in a relationship, have you noticed a complete absence of sexual fantasies or any urge to masturbate since you lost weight?
I haven't really thought about that or noticed it, to be honest. My mind has been entirely consumed by food, my weight, and my work lately, so those things haven't even crossed my mind.
Have you noticed your skin becoming unusually dry, or have you experienced any thinning or loss of the hair on your head since you started losing weight?
I haven't really noticed any unusual dryness in my skin or thinning of my hair. My focus has just been completely on keeping my body as lean as possible and managing my daily routine.
